record.context_brief: Finiteness in the Markov spectrum of decomposable forms
record.original_question: For every ε>0, is the set [ε,∞)∩{m(F)} finite, where m(F) is the normalized Markov minimum of a decomposable ternary form F?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 41 (G. Margulis). Show that for every ε > 0, the set [ε, ∞ ) ∩ {m(F )} is ﬁnite.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A decomposable ternary form is a homogeneous polynomial $F(x_1,x_2,x_3) \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,x_2,x_3]$ that factors as a product of (real or complex) linear forms over $\mathbb{C}$. For such a form $F$, define its normalized Markov minimum by
$$m(F) \;=\; \frac{\inf\{\,|F(v)| : v \in \mathbb{Z}^3 \setminus \{0\}\,\}}{|\mathrm{disc}(F)|^{1/d}},$$
where $d = \deg F$ and the normalization makes $m(F)$ invariant under $\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and under scalar rescaling of $F$. Let
$$\mathcal{M} \;=\; \{\, m(F) : F \text{ a decomposable ternary form with } m(F)>0\,\}$$
be the associated Markov spectrum.

Prove or disprove: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, the set $[\varepsilon, \infty) \cap \mathcal{M}$ is finite.

Related work concerns Margulis's results on values of indefinite ternary quadratic forms (Oppenheim conjecture) and moments of Margulis functions, but no source found directly establishes or refutes finiteness of $[\varepsilon,\infty)\cap\{m(F)\}$ for decomposable ternary forms. Status appears unverified from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Moments of Margulis functions and indefinite ternary quadratic forms
status_evidence.snippet: Uniform bounds on moments of Margulis functions used in quantitative results about values of indefinite ternary quadratic forms.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on related quantitative problems for ternary forms exists, but does not address the decomposable-form Markov spectrum finiteness question.

status_evidence.title: The Geometry of Numbers on a Quadric Surface (W. Duke)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Markov-type spectra in the setting of ternary forms.
status_evidence.claim: Background on Markov spectra in higher rank, but no resolution of the specific finiteness conjecture above is found.
